build:net-driver-legality.notes:
Extended NetResolutionSimulator with the three new labs the spec asks for. All existing presets, props, exports and tests still work, and the component still takes no props when embedded bare.

**New props and where they lead**
- `initialMode` ('drivers' | 'legality' | 'trireg') picks the starting mode. If it is omitted and `pattern` is set, the component opens in legality mode.
- Legality mode now has a "Legality lab" switch with three views: "Whole variable" (the old lab, still the default), "Bits of logic [1:0] v" and "Port kinds". `pattern` selects the second or third.
- `preset='open-drain'` opens the open-drain view inside drivers mode. Any other existing preset id loads that corner case. A new "Open-drain on tri1" button means the default embed can reach it too.

**Model changes (sv-four-state-model.ts, all additive)**
- `WriterKind` gains 'initializer'. `Writer` gains an optional `bits: [hi, lo]`.
- On a variable, an initializer counts as a procedural write (§6.5). On a net it is a net declaration assignment, which is continuous (§10.3.1).
- `checkDrivers(decl, writers, {width, name})` checks each bit on its own and returns `bits` (MSB first) and `flaggedBits`.
- Called without ranges or width, `checkDrivers` behaves as before, plus a single `bits` entry.
- New outcomes:
  - 'no-writer': nothing writes the bit.
  - 'tool-dependent': an initializer plus always_comb or always_ff on the same bit. §6.5 treats the initializer as procedural, and §9.2.2.2 only forbids writes

Verified, no S1/S2 in this group. IEEE 1800-2023 §10.3.4 says a drive strength pair has one strength for 1 and one for 0, in either order, from supply/strong/pull/weak/highz. It makes (highz1, highz0) and (highz0, highz1) illegal and defaults to (strong1, strong0). checkStrengthPair at src/lib/sv-four-state-model.ts:566 and effectiveDriver at :588 match this. The model stores the pair as (s0, s1), so both illegal orderings collapse to one check. Table 28-7 puts highz0 and highz1 at level 0, and STRENGTH_LEVEL at :515 matches all 8 levels. §28.3.2 says nor (highz1,strong0) 'outputs a z in place of a 1', which agrees with effectiveDriver turning a 1 at highz1 into z. Running the model confirmed this: (strong0, highz1) driving 1 returns z, and on a wire next to a weak 0 the net resolves to We0 with only b counted. A 0 at highz0 also returns z. strength1 alone with a 1 driven gives the 1 at that strength. An equal-strength x passes through. (highz0, highz1) throws even for a z value. driverAssignSource with no per-value strengths emits (strong0, strong1), and the component's d() helper and its new-driver button default to strong, so the default stays (strong0, strong1). The only modelled nets are scalar and none are supply0/supply1, which agrees with the §10.3.4 scope sentence. The UI cannot reach the throwing paths: the open-drain view only drives 0 or 1, and drivers mode has no per-value strength control. vitest: 103/103 pass across the two test files.
